headline: Dozens walked out on Netanyahu. He kept going.
summary: Dozens of delegates left the hall as Benjamin Netanyahu rose to address the UN General Assembly on Thursday. He called them moral cowards and defended Israel's wars in Gaza and Iran: "We're going to win. We have no other choice." He rejected the charge of genocide in Gaza, where the Hamas-run health ministry counts more than 73,920 dead.

cover_question.q: Why did they walk out on him?

cover_answer: Protest over Gaza. He called them moral cowards.
table_question: Is walking out on a speech braver than staying to argue?

5-7.script: A leader from a country called Israel gave a speech at a big meeting of countries in New York, and lots of people walked out before he started. They did it to show they're upset about a war far away. It's like leaving the table when someone says something you think is wrong. You're safe, and the grown-ups are working on it.
5-7.why: The walkout is the whole story at six. The war stays far away and unnamed, which is where it belongs.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old is frightened by what they can picture, so the script keeps the war far away and unnamed and puts the walkout, a thing people did with their feet, in front. Leaving the table is the anchor: a protest they have made themselves. Expect "is the war coming here?" No. It is far away, and you are safe.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: Every leader gets a turn at the UN. When Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu stood up, dozens of delegates walked out over the war in Gaza. He called them moral cowards. A walkout is a team refusing to shake hands: the score stays, but everyone sees it.
8-12.why: One turn, one refusal. The handshake gives them the protest without the war.
8-12.why_long: This age is sorting out rules and whether people follow them, so the script gives them the rule first: one microphone, one turn each. The handshake is the walkout: a refusal that changes nothing on the scoreboard but everyone sees. Expect "who's right?" Say that people who study this disagree, and that is why they were at the UN.

13-17.script: Is walking out an argument, or a refusal to have one? Dozens left as Netanyahu took the stage; he called them moral cowards. Second: a court wants him arrested for war crimes, and the UN gave him the microphone. Should it have?
13-17.why: Two questions they can take either side of. Let them argue before you do.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things: a walkout is a statement and also a refusal to hear the other side, and a leader can be wanted by one court and still be handed the UN's microphone. The script states the genocide charge with who says what. Expect "which side are you on?" Answer honestly, then ask them to make the other case first.

5-7.q: Why did people leave the room?
5-7.a: They were upset about a war and wanted him to know it. Leaving quietly is one way grown-ups say they disagree.

8-12.q: Can they make him stop the war?
8-12.a: No. A walkout is only a message. He said Israel will fight until it wins.
The Palestinian president. Denied a US visa, he spoke by video and said Israel threatens his people.

13-17.q: Why did they walk out on him?
13-17.a: Protest over Gaza. A UN inquiry has accused Israel of genocide there. Israel denies it.
A UN inquiry and genocide scholars say yes. Israel says self-defence.
